Researchers seek to derive a single representation capable of capturing the essence of musical input from various sources, including sheet music, song lyrics, and audio. This study addresses the challenge of unified representation learning across multiple input formats. To this end, a new music dataset, named MusicTM-Dataset, was created by leveraging Music21 and Madagascar music tools for sheet music and audio analysis. The dataset comprises three main parts: musical notes, lyrics, and audio spectra, all aligned through index systems. Five powerful neural network models, each optimized for specific input formats, were developed and tested, revealing their respective strengths and weaknesses. Notably, a transformer-based multi-task neural network outperformed other models in the given benchmark experiments. The MusicTM-Dataset and accompanying code were made available for public access.

For complex datasets, visual representations can facilitate exploration and assist users in forming informed queries using specific languages. Ontoforce is a tool that helps developers integrate natural language support into data visualization systems, enabling users to frame queries in English and receive visual results. Ontoforce was initially developed to enhance the Ontodia graph visualization platform, allowing users to submit English queries and view the resulting composite views. Currently, Ontoforce includes an English-to-SparQL translator and a set of predefined English keywords that users can employ to construct queries. This research builds upon Ontoforce by addressing its limitations in several key areas. Firstly, the project's current translation method is basic and solely supports English. We will demonstrate how word embeddings can be utilized to expand support to multiple languages. Secondly, the project's dictionary is relatively tiny, comprising only 115 English keywords. We will showcase three innovative methodologies - concept similarity, sequence matching, and entity prediction - that enable a more natural English query formulation. Finally, the project's current translation algorithm is simplistic and cannot accurately model complex English sentences. We will illustrate two ways - sequence-to-sequence generation and sentence refinement - to utilize word embeddings in Ontofac to generate more sophisticated SparQL queries based on English sentences.

We investigate the properties of dark solitons in models of the optical nonlinear Schrödinger equation, specifically considering cases where the medium's dispersion is influenced by intensity. Our study focuses on two main models: the ones featuring cubic and quintic interactions. For both models, when the external light source is sufficiently weak, the models exhibit the same characteristics as the well-known cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. As the external light source's power increases, the quintic model displays an unusual shift in the soliton's position, unlike in the cubic case. Additionally, by making a connection between the dark soliton and its bright counterpart, we gain new insights into the behavior of dark solitons in optical systems.

(Research paper abstract) 
To address the rising challenge of joint inferences between human and machine, we are developing a novel system that seamlessly integrates lotteries of different services. Our system, SeLA, assists in setting up these competitions between human and machine predictions. We are also introducing Lotse, a functional framework that facilitates the effortless creation of various task-specific collaboration methods, allowing for multiple-established competition mechanisms to be reconfigured as inverse auctions. Through our experience with building Lotse, we have discovered that, given a particular task, various method configurations can often be developed simultaneously. Our work has implications on both human-computer interaction and software design, influencing how developers allocate computational resources and prioritize human involvement.

An innovative method has been developed to strengthen the quasisymmetry and nested structure of stellarator designs through the integration of coil enhancements, which are strategically placed nested coils, often located outside the primary coil set. Utilizing the IPF quasisymmetric design as a foundation, our research demonstrates that incorporating two specific coil enhancements, arranged in opposite directions, can maintain stellarator characteristics with minimal deviation. By optimizing the position and size of these enhancements, stellarator configurations with preserved quasisymmetry and nested structures can be achieved, even allowing for significant variations in magnetic field strength. Additionally, our research shows that stellarator configurations based on the IPF design can effectively allow for plasma rotation while preserving quasisymmetry, a distinctive feature compared to other stellarator designs. Furthermore, our study examines the M3D-C1 code's simulations of these enhanced stellarator configurations, demonstrating that they exhibit well-behaved magnetic field profiles and provide extensive action areas for efficient plasma confinement.

Achieving uniform temperature within industrial reactors is of paramount importance, making temperature control a major challenge. In the past few years, the utilization of hyperpolarized gas magnetic resonance imaging has opened up new possibilities for studying temperature in these systems. In the course of high-temperature fluidized bed reactions, as a result of rising products, temperature fluctuations can be created, prompting the quest for an advanced thermal management and mixing technique. In this study, the temperature fluctuations in a bed of glass particles caused by gas flow rates being periodically increased and decreased was investigated using rapid in situ MRI. Three distinct regimes were identified as a result of this analysis, characterized by different values of the Reynolds number and temperature differences between the gas and solid phases. Furthermore, four distinct modes of heat transfer were observed and their physical properties were explained, where unique phenomena were observed in the case of laminar fluid dynamics. In addition to this, the temperature differences were found to be relatively small, prompting the utilization of the Munson correction formula to ensure accurate determination of the vertical temperature gradient.

A primary issue in statistical physics has been to explain spontaneous symmetry breaking in physical systems, which has recently been tackled by applying a similar framework to biological systems. The inherent symmetry in some biomolecular aggregates, such as some lipids and proteins, is broken due to structural disparities in their constituent elements, resulting in unique structures. However, a new theoretical approach suggests that the diversity in these elements is sufficient to generate aggregates with inherent symmetries, without necessarily forming a crystal lattice structure. Computer simulations confirm that membranes composed of molecules with three different types of lipids can still exhibit spontaneous curvature preferences, even though there are no crystalline structures involved. This suggests a common connection between thermal agitation, inherent preferences in curvature, and the general geometrical properties of aggregates, which can explain numerous examples of spontaneous curvature preferences in various structures, such as cells and membranes.

On August 29-30, 2012, NOAA AR 11429 underwent a major transformation characterized by two significant sunspot revolts occurring approximately 90 minutes apart. This phenomenon is unusually rare, particularly in major sunspot areas. The sudden emergence of two intense solar flares, a X1.5 and an M7.6 event, triggered by the massive eruptions associated with these revolts, further highlights the importance of these events in understanding the complex magnetohydrodynamic processes that govern major solar activity. The rapid development and evolution of the revolts were fueled by highly turbulent movements in localized shear shears, which led to the disruption of a highly twisted magnetic structure via numerous stress accumulation and release episodes. The resultant disturbances had a significant impact on the solar crust, triggering radio bursts, solar impurities, and a rapid increase in the solar wind speed. The corresponding reduction in the sun's chromospheric and corona temperatures was relatively short-lived, approximately one day, before temperatures returned to pre-event levels. The rapid cooling was likely induced by the stressor-related disturbances propagating down to the solar surface, causing significant energy dissipation. The rapid cooling was accompanied by the development of a short-lived forward shock, a short-lived forward shock, and a type II radio burst, which further highlights the stressor-related disturbances having an impact on the solar atmosphere, ultimately being carried down to the solar surface, and eventually triggering a type IV radio emission.

We have summarized the key outcomes of the b-principle, recently established by Abdurahmanović, Mendes Gomes, and Rovi, in simplified terms. Building upon this framework, a new theorem is developed to demonstrate that a particular moduli space's virtual fundamental class can be rigorously defined, under the conditions specified by the Mumford hypothesis.

Cardiac tissue mechanics can be modeled using the partial differential equations (PDEs) resulting from the conservative Lagrangian, but these equations are non-linear and require expansion through time. Linearizations of these equations via the discrete tangent space, formed by combining finite element displacements and velocities, enable the use of iterative solvers like GMRES with significant memory savings over traditional approaches. Two multilevel preconditioning methods for GMRES are presented, differing in the construction of the discrete tangent space. An analytical inspection of these approaches, supported by numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, indicates that both methods demonstrate efficient convergence and reduced memory usage, making them suitable for use in cardiac mechanics applications.

The ever-growing influence of social media is primarily attributed to the inherent collaborative features inherent in them, which foster user engagement and creativity. This research delves into the intricacies of user collaboration in social tagging systems, which are present almost everywhere online today. To uncover the underlying dynamics of these systems, we developed a mathematical model based on a unique time-based approach and our findings reveal a complex interplay between user reusage, time, user interest shifting, and the establishment of both informal and formal online relationships. Our results, which align with empirical data from the well-known Del.icio.us system, offer novel insights into the subtle social interactions taking place within these systems, which are instrumental in understanding user collaboration in social tagging systems.

Recently, researchers have devised a technique using traditional lithography to produce acoustic metagratings with unprecedented properties. These structures, made possible by traditional lithography methods, can manipulate acoustic waves in ways natural gratings cannot, including generating multiple out-of-plane reflections and flexible angle conversions. However, their typical operating frequencies are relatively low, ranging from kilohertz to a few tens of kilohertz. This paper presents an innovative approach using two-photon lithography to produce advanced microacoustic metagratings that work at much higher frequencies, over a range from 10,000 to 40,000 hertz. The technique involves designing hexagonal structures with specific phase-shift properties that redirect sound waves efficiently. The results show that these novel microacoustic metagratings provide efficient conversions in both theory and experimental settings, with conversions as high as 90% in some cases.

This paper explores the behavior of the 2-D compressible FENE dumbbell model, particularly its solution's longevity and long-term trends in different scenarios. By establishing a useful estimate, we demonstrate that the solution can endure any time period in certain circumstances. In other cases, with a slightly stronger initial condition, the solution is shown to be valid for a minimum amount of time. In both situations, the trajectory of the solution converges to a steady state as time progresses, but the rate of convergence varies significantly. Notably, the time it takes for the solution to reach a steady state is proportional to the inverse of the Reynolds number and the logarithm of the Strouhal number, plus a constant (all divided by a specific viscosity value). This long-term trend shares many similarities with that of the incompressible FENE dumbbell model's solution.

Implementing Implementing IAB (Intrinsic Abort) on mobile devices is complicated due to limitations in current microcontrollers. Current research primarily focuses on the application of IAB in mobile devices but doesn't thoroughly explore the underlying difficulties. This work aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and proposed solutions in integrating IAB into mobile devices for DRAM memory. We begin by explaining the concept of IAB, identifying the issues related to its application on mobile devices, and describing the proposed solutions. Moreover, we outline potential obstacles and areas for further research.

In optimization, ranking methods successfully manage diverse results produced by multiple algorithms with different settings, contributing to algorithmic research and experimentation. However, the effectiveness of ranking schemes is influenced by various factors, including how well their hyperparameters are optimized. Unfortunately, a comprehensive study connecting ranking scheme hyperparameters to performance is lacking, making it challenging to select suitable ranking methods and parameters for specific tasks. To address this, we investigated the sensitivity of ranking schemes to their hyperparameters in order to gain insights into their interactions. By conducting extensive experiments across 18 tasks from varied domains, we evaluated the sensitivity of 16 ranking schemes representing six different families, using three global optimization algorithms. Our research reveals significant opportunities for future research, including the development of more informed algorithm selection methods, as well as the potential for hyperparameter transfer between ranking schemes, suggesting a need to develop more nuanced and adaptive ranking algorithms that learn from the strengths of their components.

We examine the fundamental wave equation in one dimension, specifically the Schrödinger equation, with the aim of establishing a set of principles that align with the Born rule. This will involve deriving a set of preconditions for the wave function, which must be satisfied for the Born rule to be applicable. These preconditions serve as a framework for theoretical wave function interpretations and provide a set of principles that align with the use of wave functions in quantum mechanics. This work builds on previous research, which established a set of principles for complex probability amplitudes, and expands upon it by considering the relationship between these amplitudes and the volume they belong to.

To establish a benchmark for future research and study the limitations of current Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches, we introduce the $L^2$ Explorer, a platform that continuously evaluates agents in dynamic environments. The platform is designed to be versatile, allowing researchers to investigate various research questions in areas such as bounded rationality, partial observability, multi-agent learning, and more. The current evaluation of the platform includes a thorough analysis of state-of-the-art DRL agents on classic benchmark domains like Montezuma Revenge, Montezuma Reward, and more. The $L^2$ Explorer's source code and experimental data are publicly available, enabling replication and facilitating future research submissions.

Liger is a next-generation infrared device that will be utilized on the Keck telescopes, featuring its exceptional sensitivity and imaging capabilities over a broad wavelength range stretching from 1.7 micrometers to 5.2 micrometers. Liger's vast field of view will be composed of 7.9 x 5.2 arcseconds, encompassing up to 12,900 pixels, with a sub-twenty micrometer resolution. To effectively process and analyze the immense amount of data that Liger will generate during its observations, there has been significant development in the device's software and data processing system. This paper outlines the progress made in these areas of research, including a connection between the Liger data reduction software and an extensive astronomical database that provides information on celestial objects, thereby enhancing the accuracy of Liger's data outputs.

We examine traveling wave solutions of the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation in a planar wave background, with no fluid flow in the reference state. These solutions are perturbed with an irregular force and we observe that for certain conditions regarding the regularity and decay rate of the solution, as well as the strength of the force, a traveling wave close to the initial state will emerge. This is in accordance with a broader understanding that was first proposed by Esposito, Kowalczyk, and Vecchiello.

We experimentally control linear polarization of photon-polariton condensates using optical methods. Our research shows that, depending on the optical stimulation power, linear polarization switching can be achieved in two ways: either by a sudden shift (in a phenomenon known as "all-optical switching"), or through a more gradual change (in a process called "light-pattern writing"). Additionally, we demonstrate that linear polarization can be easily manipulated in coupled waveguide systems, even when the polarization is not maintained, by adjusting the separation between the waveguides. This study provides a foundation for developing methods to control polarization in hybrid light-matter systems and explores its applications in spin-based opto-electronics and quantum information systems.

This study's primary objective is to provide evidence and disproofs for the deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations including non-local elements with a specific structure. The specific focus lies within a particular class of non-local equations that incorporate the gradient of the solution and its power. The main highlights include the derivation of comparisons between differences in solutions and their counterparts in higher dimensions, the determination of a minimum threshold for initial data requirements, the demonstration of existence through fixed-point iterations, and the exploration of similarities and differences with the related fractional KPZ equations.

The 2019 coronavirus pandemic has caused the largest economic and social devastation in a century. South Africa, with its population of 58 million people, was one of the hardest hit countries on the African continent. To mitigate the pandemic's effects, the country implemented a Level 5 lockdown in May 2020. However, concerns arose about the economic and social implications of this measure, prompting a need to find a balance between public health and economic well-being. To address this challenge, researchers utilized machine learning algorithms to analyze publicly available data on mobility, commerce, and mobility changes to forecast daily COVID-19 cases. By leveraging Python's SciPy library, they developed an innovative forecasting approach combining forecasting and prediction skills. The results indicated that integrating mobility data with prediction skills yielded the best outcomes, with a high R-squared value of 0.877 and accurate forecasts up to 14 days, enabling data-driven decision-making during the pandemic.

We've made an improvement on a conjecture made by Freiman in 1970s regarding the sumsets. Freiman initially suspected that if A and B are subsets of Z/Zk with sumset A+B containing at least 3k - 3 elements, then for any subset C of Z/Zk with cardinality k, the intersection of (A+B) and (C+H) would not be a subset of k*Z/Zk, using the modulus k. Our recent findings validate this suspicion for all k less than or equal to 5. Our proof relies heavily on an earlier discovery made by Plumb in 2012 regarding Freiman's 3k-4 conjecture.

In medical fields, data fusion emerges as a crucial approach for enhancing the accuracy of diagnostic systems and new treatment methods. Combining multiple sources of information has far-reaching implications in medical imaging analysis. For ophthalmologic disciplines specifically, incorporating various modalities of medical imaging could yield significant insights into distinct eye diseases. To this end, we have investigated the use of deep learning in integrating different types of ophthalmologic imaging data, with a focus on disease diagnosis and classification. Our research entails developing a comprehensive dataset of retinal images, capturing three distinct modalities - fundus imaging, optical coherence tomography, and clinical notes - to employ deep learning and other machine learning techniques. Our findings demonstrate that fusing fundus and OCT images using deep learning can achieve exceptional results in glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy classification.

Researchers have highlighted the significance of computed tomography (CT) scans in diagnosing and assessing the severity of Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19).  A rapid diagnosis is crucial for isolating patients and preventing the spread of the virus.  Since CT scans reveal alterations in the lungs affected by COVID-19 prior to noticeable symptoms, they can serve as an essential diagnostic tool.  Researchers developed multiple datasets consisting of CT scan images of patients with varying stages of COVID-19, which has led to the creation of several classification models for lesion segmentation.  However, there is limited knowledge about the CT scan characteristics of patients admitted to Intensive Care Units (ICUs).  Therefore, this research aims to identify possible characteristics in CT images that can forecast patients' severe conditions requiring ICU admission.  To this end, researchers integrated a convolutional neural network (CNN) with capability of generating feature maps into a fully convolutional network (FCN) to segment lung regions consistently.  Then, a one-dimensional CNN was implemented to extract temporal features from image sequences, allowing for the identification of patients with severe conditions through well-designed features of temporal context.  Based on experimental results, the proposed combined network successfully segments lung regions and foresees ICU admission risks.  Moreover, the study conducted comprehensive evaluations of the proposed model and compared it with other state-of-the-art models.

This article delves into the problem of determining a spherical boundary from transmission eigenvalues or eigenfunctions in a spherically layered medium. Our initial approach resolves this issue for two-layer spheres, with distinct material properties in the outer and inner layers, where we derive an infinite-dimensional algebraic equation for the boundary. Our second method tackles the general case of a multilayered sphere comprising several materials with varying layers. Utilizing the Wronskian formula, we develop conditions to calculate the boundary at which transmission eigenfunctions terminate. Our analysis provides a degree-of-determination result, showing that each layer's boundary can be individually identified from the given information. Our results are validated by numerical simulations.

A target detection intent in sonar is commonly characterized by a series of signal peaks in varying depths, and the depth of these peaks serves as a key feature for classification purposes. The challenge lies in detecting the peaks from noisy sonar data and using the depth information to differentiate between intentions. The proposed approach leverages a pre-trained network for feature extraction and a comparison metric for comparing sequences. The network's output features are then fed into a classification layer and a regression layer, trained together, to optimize the result. The method has been tested on Inmarsat sonar data and shows promising results.
We establish that the global simplicial bundle, as defined by Dwyer--Kan--Kalker, constitutes a simplicial structure.

Let $G$ be a finite group with $n$ elements, and consider any division of $G$ into non-empty subsets, denoted as $G_1,\dots,G_k$, where the groups $G_i$ have an equal number of elements, each being $n/k$. We establish that the total number of these subgroups does not exceed $2^{\frac{n}{k}\log_2(G)+k}$. This inequality holds true for all possible divisions of the group $G$ into $G_1,\dots,G_k$. We find that the upper limit is reached if $k$ is a prime number that divides the order of $G$. Moreover, the result implies an exponential upper bound on the number of distinct subgroups of a finite group $G$, given by $2^{k\frac{n}{k}\log_2(G)}$.

The Barnes-type $2J2$ identity was first introduced by H.S. Barnes in 1937, and
recently, the general form of the formula has been referred to as the ABS H2 formula.
Originally, the proof involved combinatorial analysis, but the equation has
since been reinterpreted in terms of cluster algebras, and an explicit formula has
been developed to express $2J2$ as a product of hyperbolic 4-cluster complexes.
This paper examines the underlying structure of the formula, and provides a
detailed examination of the components, starting from the permutation group $S_n$,
via Aztec diamonds, and arriving at the explicit formula recently derived by M. Hytonen, 
in relation to the signed permutation networks defined by M. Hytonen, J. Korondo, 
and T. Laitinen.

This study addresses the problem of false positives in visual association detection, a task where two images are labeled as paired when humans consider them associated. We're working on developing indicators to measure the likelihood of false positives in association data. These indicators include human agreements on whether the second image is not part of the first image's visual context, the presence of additional information that can rectify mislabeled pairs, and the utilization of high-level image features. We evaluate existing benchmarks and our newly collected dataset, Emergent Associations Anthology (EAA), through the lens of these indicators, proposing new benchmarks for association data quality assessment.

We investigate the effect of weak measurement's associated expense within the context of the continuous-time quantum random walk. Underneath specific circumstances, we demonstrate that the associated expense exhibits a non-local, entanglement-based property. Additionally, we examine the associated expense when the measurement's strength is adjusted. Our analysis explores the associated expense's dynamic behavior following a change in its point of interest and the influence of multiple weak measurements.

The rise of social relationship mining has led to a growing demand for accurate networks representing interpersonal connections. Nonetheless, there is still a pressing need for a reliable resource of social relationship graphs (SRGs) due to the absence of sufficient data available for public use. To address this gap, we have developed an extensive network of SRGs for individuals and organizations across five diverse domains: academic, artistic, economic, political, and sporting. Our comprehensive dataset encompasses over 4 million entities and 170 million edge connections, encompassing global data from five distinct categories. We have implemented an innovative approach to create high-quality networks of SRGs through the combination of existing datasets, web scraping techniques, and manual verification. Our method has specific advantages that enable the creation of high-quality networks, including the adaptation of node merging and entity disambiguation techniques to optimize the accuracy and reliability of our datasets. Additionally, we have developed a straightforward formula to determine the strength of connections between interconnected entities, facilitating the creation of high-quality SRGs. Our comprehensive network of SRGs and associated data can be utilized for various applications, including relationship mining, information gathering, research, and content creation. The entire process of creating these networks and the underlying data has been documented in detail, enabling seamless reproduction of our results by other researchers. Our work has significant practical value, providing a valuable reference for anyone seeking to create high-quality social relationship graphs.

This research introduces a novel Dynamic Graph Message Network (DGN), which is a neural network architecture designed to identify moving objects in a visual sequence. The DGN is constructed by aggregating multiple message passing modules, allowing it to effectively capture object movements across multiple frames. A specific module type, the attention message pass module, is introduced, which uses a attention mechanism to facilitate message aggregation and enable graph edge selection. By dynamic graph convolutional layer (DGC) processing, the DGN is able to leverage contextual information related to node connections within the graph. Notably, the DGN is capable of handling complex and diverse data, yielding impressive results in benchmark tests for multiple applications, including human pose prediction, hand keystone detection, and vehicle tracking.

Resource optimization in Digital Signal Processing systems is heavily influenced by Common Multiplications and various forms of Constant Multiplications which can be viewed as a special type of multiplication. A new approach has been developed to efficiently use resources in designs involving Constant Multiplications by optimizing the hardware cost. Initial testing on actual ICs has shown the proposed method can cut resource usage by up to 80% compared to traditional designs.

The burgeoning fields of Quantum Machine Learning and Quantum Neural Networks are receiving significant attention, with researchers developing novel approaches that seamlessly integrate quantum computing with deep learning. This research field is still in its early stages and thus lacking in comprehensive summaries of its core concepts and recent breakthroughs. To address this gap, we provide an in-depth review of quantum neural networks, covering fundamental ideas, recent advancements in algorithms and applications, as well as challenges and potential future directions.

High-energy particle physics programs require robust Radio Frequency (RF) systems to accelerate and counteract magnetic fields in Particle Accelerators. A specialized RF booster is needed to boost the energy of already accelerated particles for specific experiments. A study group for RF Systems participated in the 2021 Snowmass program and investigated challenges, opportunities, and potential developments in RF booster technology. This document outlines the study group's findings and recommendations.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles, compares different collider designs with varying energy specifications, magnetic material options, and provides an overview of the current status of research and potential hurdles associated with the development of a muon collider.

We have developed an expression to predict gravitational waves generated by cosmic events involving relativistic fluids and gravity, based on an approach that builds upon numerical simulations in relativistic fluid dynamics. By combining this expression with numerical data from such simulations, we have created a predictive model of gravitational waves. The model accounts for the impact of viscosity, in addition to the traditional elements of relativistic fluids, and is formulated in a way that's easily applicable to numerical simulations. By doing so, we have made it possible to incorporate the effects of viscosity into relativistic fluid dynamics without introducing additional complexity, and with a model that's both flexible and versatile.

Our research assesses whether primordial black holes serving as radioactive sources could be responsible for the diffuse radio background measured by ARCADE2 and PRIZMA. We used the code COSMOPIG to model the radio sky at cosmological frequencies, with the latter featuring an unusual dipolar pattern. This phenomenon might be attributed to an uneven cosmic microwave background radiation, but our findings indicate that it can be entirely explained by radiation emitted by primordial black holes with a mass fraction of PBHs relative to dark matter being in the 10^-3 to 10^-4 range. Primordial black holes with a mass of approximately 10^14 grams and a higher mass fraction of dark matter would result in a radio background excess compared to the observed value, while those with a lower mass fraction of dark matter would result in a radio background strength smaller than the observed value. We determined the range of possible PBH mass spectra that could be consistent with data, with estimated mass fractions of dark matter accounted for when the PBH mass is between 10^12 and 10^16 grams.

Introducing the Virtual Safe Framework (VSF), a pioneering system that brings together multi-processor architecture and homogeneous execution of arbitrary programs on Protected Multiplication Circuits, thereby achieving exact zero-knowledge proofs capable of encompassing a wide scope of program activity. At the heart of VSF lies the Virtual Safe, a novel symmetric construct that facilitates the safe execution of programs in the relatively less complex Rational Number world, thereby enabling the conversion of program code into suitable Circuit representations. Furthermore, VSF's unique architecture allows programs to be divided into distinct modules executed on different processors, with each module responsible for a particular program stage. By decentralizing program modules across multiple processors and utilizing a modular approach, VSF significantly boosts computation speed compared to a single-processor architecture. To underscore its robustness, VSF has been put through various functional and performance tests, including an impressive custom-built multi-processor prototype consisting of five processors that demonstrated the successful execution of up to five program stages in just 14.35 milliseconds.

Researchers have developed various methods to solve CSPs more efficiently by exploiting problem structure. Their work has a direct connection to efficient approximation algorithms for related NP-hard problems with specific constraints. The study focuses on general weighted CSPs, proposing a new algorithm that combines concise descriptions of problem structures with precise linear programming models. Due to the absence of suitable tractable restrictions, the team developed a new approach consisting of a polynomial-time algorithm for constructing a restricted linear programming model and a sequence of progressively smaller LP-problems to obtain a near-optimal solution within a certain gap. By integrating this algorithm with techniques for solving CSPs over finite domains, the team obtained a quasi-PAS with a runtime complexity of O(2^(2nn^2) log 2nn). After that, the team designed a PTAS consisting of two components. The first involves constructing a specific linear programming model based on problem structure descriptions and solution candidates with a particular characteristic. The second component uses techniques similar to those in Xie's LP-GAC algorithm to obtain a near-optimal solution. Finally, the team applied techniques from LP relaxation with constrained optimization to develop a new algorithm, obtaining a PTAS with runtime complexity of O(n^4.76).

In this research, we investigate whether pre-trained language models can achieve top-notch performance in tasks that don't require extensive training data and are not accompanied by supplementary information. Our study reveals that these models perform exceptionally well at a range of unsupervised and little-example tasks, such as sentence duplication, reversing order, and removing phrases. Notably, they achieve state-of-the-art results on the Natural Language Inference and Sentential Inference tasks and perform remarkably well on the Fake or Not dataset for limited-example data. Our experiments also reveal that the GPT-2 model's performance is enhanced by its capacity to process text sequentially rather than in a single, comprehensive feed. Our source code is freely accessible at https://github.com/ghboldi/unsupvised-lm.

Understanding a city's infrastructure from a bird's perspective is crucial for city planning and design. Although AI can generate detailed 3D city models, creating accurate segmentations for architectural, vegetation, and man-made areas is an ongoing challenge. Existing methods rely on high-resolution 2D images or LiDAR data, but these segments don't translate well to 3D models. Moreover, manually creating such categories is time-consuming and labor-intensive. In response to this challenge, a new approach called HyperCity, uses hyperspectral imagery to create cityscape segments. The process involves collecting spectral features, selecting relevant bands using dimensionality reduction, and clustering these features to create categories. The technique is weakly-supervised, relying on global image structures rather than local details, which helps extend its applications to areas with limited data. The method shows promising results and outperforms traditional approaches in accuracy. The associated code and dataset are available for public use.

The unique architecture of our solar system's outer planets is a result of a complex series of events that occurred early in the sun's formation. A recent study suggests that a massive gas particle with a mass similar to that of Jupiter might have played a significant role in shaping the planetary positions. This particle, moving at high speeds, would have transferred its angular momentum to the protoplanetary disk, potentially explaining the observed spacings between the outer planets. However, a simpler explanation could be that this particle interacted with one or more planets, causing them to spin rapidly. A new study examines the spin rates of Uranus and Neptune to determine which scenario is more plausible.

We examine the interconnection between the fastest known algorithms for linear equations, inverse problems, and combinatorial issues within the RAM model that utilizes addition. Our investigation demonstrates that in the RAM model with addition, the following statements are equivalent to linear equation solving having a constant time complexity: 1) Comb's problem has a constant time complexity, 2) the factorial calculation has a constant time complexity, 3) the greatest common divisor (GCD) operation has a constant time complexity, 4) the modular inverse problem has a constant time complexity, 5) matrix inversion in 2x2 matrices has a constant time complexity, and 6) the polynomial coefficient calculation has a constant time complexity. Additionally, we find that in the RAM model with addition, the operations of logarithmic overhead for prime decomposition and modular inverse are necessary and sufficient. Our study is based on a thorough analysis of a new, general technique for linear equation solving in the RAM model with addition.

To tackle the data sparsity problem in session-based recommendation, a new approach using graph co-training is introduced in the paper. This method leverages user-item interactions encoded in a graph to enhance cold-start predictions in recommendation systems. Building on the success of co-training, which leverages dual networks utilizing mutually reinforced input data, the graph co-training approach adapts this technique to session-based recommendation. In the proposed system, two separate models process self-guided graph information and shared data to produce complementary results. The graph component enables the learning of session-based preferences from user and item historical behavior. The proposed algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in various settings, with significant enhancements of over 30% in the best-case scenario.

The concept of reversible source encoding (RSE) serves as a means to quantify the inherent irreversibility present in any source encoding method, with the least reversible source entropy representing this irreversibility. A new type of code, known as the group reversible LCM code, is proposed, which is capable of achieving the least reversible source entropy for certain ergodic source channels based on a finite group. Additionally, properties and decoding algorithms for RSE in relation to group reversible LCM codes have been studied. Furthermore, an example is provided to demonstrate the efficacy of group reversible LCM codes.

Differential forms provide a powerful mathematical approach to extend network concepts, making it possible to relate complex geometry to electric current and topological quantities. This framework has an inherent advantage over traditional methods, as it remains unaffected by scale changes. Our study demonstrates the application of this framework to various quantities derived from network shape, including Feynman integrals.

In various studies, researchers have demonstrated that object recognition in monkeys and higher animals, as well as in self-learning neural networks, relies heavily on localized visual processing regions.  Despite the abundance of evidence, the underlying mechanism of interaction between visual processing areas remains largely unclear.  To shed light on this, the authors proposed a novel training protocol for a recurrent neural network using double stimuli to differentiate between objects.  Through analysis of the network's internal state transitions, the study revealed that the network employs temporal summation of distinct visual characteristics to distinguish between objects, thereby utilizing category-orthogonal visual properties to facilitate processing.  Interestingly, the network's temporal processing capabilities exceeded its spatial capabilities, with performance improving when using stimuli organized sequentially rather than simultaneously.  These findings align with previous findings on object recognition in monkeys and highlight the significance of sequential processing in advanced visual tasks.

In one-dimensional non-Hermitian systems with a point gap, the imaginary part of the spectral density at the point gap (phased jump) is essentially an local interaction effect, independent of its remote action. This phenomenon is equally present in both Hermitian systems and one-dimensional non-Hermitian systems with a band gap. By using a mathematical approach based on Green's function, the phasing mechanism is explained in terms of the balance between the system's bulk and edge states. Additionally, an applicable mathematical formula is provided. Our research also highlights the causal relationship between the imaginary part of the potential and the point gap's phasing. Furthermore, our results are substantiated through two practical models, a tight-binding model and a massless Dirac model. Our findings have crucial implications for the field of one-dimensional non-Hermitian topology, opening up new avenues for reducing the requirements of multi-terminal electronic devices, such as those needed for ideal single-photoelectron sources, by converting them into single-terminal devices that respond electronically to light.

This research proposes a novel ring-orientated ring array architecture known as the polyphase Golay complementary structure, which is based on the Golay complementary sequence. The paper initially explains the concept of Golay complementary Sequences and its properties before outlining a method to create a synchro-oriented ring array using these sequences. The proposed PCA structures have the ability to generate identical phase-shifted outputs for multiple clock signals, making them suitable for direct implementation in integrated circuits and system-on-chip designs. Additionally, the paper demonstrates the feasibility of generating hexagonal PCA structures with enhanced inter-ring connectivity, which can run at higher frequencies compared to traditional ring-based architectures. By analyzing the phase-shifted output spectra of these PCA structures, it is shown that they produce minimal crosstalk and interference with other circuits. Due to their potential applications in integrated circuits and system-on-chip designs, the proposed PCA structures present an advantage over traditional ring-based architectures.

New, more precise tests are needed to assess the Higgs boson's anomalous properties, specifically its broadness and connections with $VV$ processes. This is fueled by recent findings indicating the Higgs boson's broadness could be on the order of 10% if its mass is around 125 GeV, far exceeding the theoretical predictions related to vacuum stability. This paper explores the potential of using the CSO (CMS) and ATLAS experiments' four-lepton final states to develop more accurate assessments, specifically off-shell and on-shell $HH$ production, focusing on the former. The study demonstrates that combining off-shell and on-shell searches for $HH$ can lead to the determination of the Higgs boson's broadness and unusual $HVV$ connections with a 95% confidence interval of approximately $\sigma_{br^2}(HH) < 0.13$ GeV, a substantial improvement that this method can achieve in the near future, a 3-order magnitude improvement over current data and future data from the LHC Run II.

Hyperspectral imaging technology, characterized by high spectral resolution, enables in-depth analysis of objects and their alterations in various contexts, such as environmental monitoring, agriculture, and food safety. To enhance processing efficiency and address the complexity of hyperspectral images, a novel technique using deep convolutional autoencoders is developed to identify alterations without human annotation. This approach leverages transfer learning to derive spatial features from a pre-trained model, combines them with a custom-designed autoencoder that integrates encoders with a fusion module, and uses GoogleNet's classification module as the representative discriminator. To train the model in an unsupervised manner, an altered version of the contrastive loss is proposed, incorporating a reconstruction loss and a contrastive loss with reduced input data. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through experiments on altered hyperspectral images collected from three distinct fields: land cover change, food safety, and environmental monitoring. The results show that the novel technique surpasses existing methods in terms of accuracy. The associated code is available on GitHub for reproducibility.

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial of degree $2k-1$ where $k$ is a positive integer, expressing the additive counterpart of $x^2$ on the set of integers. We examine the sequence $\mathcal{S}_{P}$ formed by the values of $P(x)$ at the integers and investigate the convergence of the modified partial sums $\mathcal{S}_{n,P}(x)$ to the function $x^2$ as $n$ approaches infinity. Specifically, for a given $x$, we analyze under which conditions $\mathcal{S}_{n,P}(x)$ converges to $x^2$ as $n$ tends to infinity and derive some necessary and sufficient conditions on the coefficients of $P(x)$. When $k$ is an even number, we explore the similarities with Fourier series and a counterexample is provided to demonstrate potential obstacles in applying existing results on convergence.

Quantum bits constructed with silicon vacancies possess great potential, 
mainly due to their inherent environmental robustness and the ability to 
link molecular systems through spin-polarized bonds. However, these quantum 
bits have a significant drawback: their valley states, which are crucial for 
molecular interactions, are highly coupled with the silicon lattice. This is 
done on purpose to facilitate molecular bonding, but unfortunately, also 
results in a loss of signal strength. Researchers have developed a new technique 
to address this issue by using local electric fields to transfer spin from 
molecules to silicon vacancies quickly. This technique, which is based on time-
dependent perturbation theory, reveals that rapid spin transfer is possible 
when the spin on a molecule is not aligned with the valley states of the 
silicon defect. In fact, rapid spin transfer occurs when the molecular spin 
is perpendicularly aligned due to reduced hybridization between the molecule 
and the silicon defect. This finding offers silicon quantum bit applications 
a significant improvement in speed and efficiency.

Our proposed open-access framework, LibOPT, is specifically designed to rapidly develop and implement various optimization strategies, empowering users to create multiple methods within a brief timeframe, demonstrating the feasibility of implementing 21 distinct techniques in just 0.8 weeks, with a total codebase size of approximately 16,000 lines. The LibOPT framework is heavily influenced by Scikit-learn, providing users with an extensive range of services, including data management, algorithmic toolsets, and hyper-parameter tuning utilities. Our in-depth numerical experiment highlights the time-saving benefits of LibOPT, comparing the development speed of our frameworks to the original research papers, showcasing significant reductions of up to $38 times$. Furthermore, our analysis demonstrates that LibOPT achieves comparable results to the original methods in diverse test cases, thus reinforcing its utility as a valuable resource for optimization research communities.

Building on Ax's work, we explore whether certain geometric properties can be inferred about polynomial equations based on their solutions in number fields and finite fields. Notably, we establish that uniform varieties with a specific geometric characteristic have solutions in affine space, and we demonstrate that algebraic tori with a particular topological property have equivalent models in any finite field extension. Additionally, we provide examples of torsors that don't have equivalent models in all finite field extensions, as well as applications of our results to studying rational point counts on family classes of uniform varieties.

In non-commutative spacetimes, quantum entities like point particles and waves may lose their defining characteristics. This investigation examines how the universal principles of non-commutativity affects all matter, including both particle and wave forms of quantum entities. A comprehensive study of a free quantum field is conducted in a non-commutative spacetime, revealing that both particle and wave states are rendered indistinguishable when governed by the fundamental principles of non-commutativity, regardless of spacetime geometry. The study further reveals that the typical methods used to describe quantum entities in spacetimes with definite geometry no longer apply in non-commutative spacetimes, leading to an identity crisis for quantum entities. Our study also shows that the parameters of non-commutativity that merge particle and wave states are not fixed by the quantum theory, as previously thought. Instead, these parameters are dictated by the black hole phase transition and the properties of the thermal bath in which the quantum entities reside.

We examine scintillation properties in 3D charge collection of synthetic single-crystalline diamond using the Two-Photon Absorption (TPA) technique. A 80 ps laser pulse with a 405 nm wavelength is applied to the diamond for one measurement, and a 532 nm laser pulse with a 10 ns duration is used for an overlapping measurement. The transient current response is studied in three-dimensional spatial conditions. The TPA coefficient is calculated based on the measured Scintillator Response Function (SRF), and our results show a relatively low TPA coefficient of (2.35 ± 0.15) cm pw^-1. A 3D charge collection map is also demonstrated in our study, which shows that the TPA technique can identify areas with photoconductive damage in the diamond. This method has potential for using the TPA coefficient as an indicator of the TPA absorption cross-section in materials, and for applying the technique to identifying defects in 3D semiconductor materials.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties have caught the attention of the Natural Language Processing (NLP) community, driving innovative research in the field. In this study, we report on the performance of our models in the inaugural Arabic Misogyny Detection challenge, where we evaluate two approaches that combine NLP tasks such as misogyny identification, hate speech classification, and off-color language recognition. Our first model tackles misogyny detection as a binary classification task, while our second model treats it as a multi-classification problem. Additionally, we analyze the characteristics of Arabic misogynous language and explore how to improve NLP systems' performance on this complex issue using data-driven and knowledge-based methods.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations, characterized by their association with a postponed generator, within a Markovian framework. Notably, the paper establishes a key comparison result, analogous to its classical stochastic counterpart, which serves as a vital tool in proving the existence of a fundamental solution. Additionally, the research demonstrates that in certain situations, the definition of a "classical solution" is comparable to that of a "marked solution".

Safety-critical systems can be protected from potential hazards using controllers designed with automatic tools, however these controllers frequently fail due to unforeseen disruptions, thereby increasing the risk of system failure, often referred to as the failure of control (FoC). This scenario is particularly concerning in autonomous driving where sudden external disturbances can induce controller failure, resulting in severe consequences for both human life and property. To address this challenge, researchers have proposed a novel approach called Resilient Model-Predictive Control (RMC), an innovative technique that integrates both safety and robustness against potential hazards into an optimized strategy. RMC achieves this goal by incorporating three key elements: an efficient reachability analysis tool, a probabilistic exploration algorithm, and a data-driven policy refinement process, all working in tandem to enhance system resilience while minimizing dependence on disturbance models. This pioneering research is the first to integrate resilience evaluation and resilience enhancement into a sequential control process, thus synthesizing a robust controller capable of adapting to unexpected disturbances in real-time, thereby protecting safe autonomous systems from failure.

A newly developed framework, referred to as the Lm mixture framework, is created to facilitate multiple distribution schemes, including the ENCODED caching scheme and Decaf scheme, which operate at various levels within the network. These schemes exploit statistical connections between distant network nodes to achieve reduced latency in network responses. The Lm mixture framework constitutes a comprehensive approach to the ENCODED caching and Decaf schemes, enabling a range of applications that are yet to be explored. To demonstrate the potential of this framework, a concrete instantiation of the Lm mixture framework, referred to as the L2 instantiation, is designed and used to improve the efficiency of distributed deep learning systems. The L2 mixture framework is built upon the principles of linear processing and Gaussian noise, and is shown to facilitate decentralized computation with memory constraints. The results show that the L2 mixture framework can support high-throughput computation over large networks with thousands of nodes without experiencing significant performance degradation.

We have expanded the Scott domain theory framework to accommodate partiality and
non-determinism in a unified structure, applicable to any univalent type theory.
Our method of analysis employs a multi-faceted evaluation algebra that
simultaneously accounts for denotations of terms, their computational meanings,
and the relationships between them, all of which are subject to the principles of
precession and approximation characteristic of domain theory. As a concrete application,
we have defined a denotational semantics for the
Pseudo-Cofunctor-Category of Partial Functions (PCF) in a univalent framework,
demonstrating that the underlying type theory's univalence implies the
familiar domain-theoretic structure of the Scott domain.

We investigate the process of pole elimination for Eisenstein series associated with $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ from the perspective of space formation. Specifically, our analysis focuses on the interrelationship between poles of Eisenstein series and the dimensions of spaces used in their composition. To understand the connections between these objects, we introduce a concept called the support pattern, which depicts the combination of spaces contributing to a Eisenstein series. Certain results regarding the growth of space volumes also facilitate our comprehension of the interdependent nature of poles and space dimensions.

A powerful framework has been developed for guaranteeing mobile robotic limb safety through the use of Control Barrier Functions.  This approach is notable for its ability to generate scalable safety mechanisms without requiring detailed system models, as well as its capacity to efficiently merge baseline control strategies with enhanced safety features.  By pooling CBFs from individual joints to address overall limb posture, our method excels at balancing operation efficiency and security.  This framework is versatile and allows security protocols to be adjusted through simple human input, giving end-users considerable control over safety settings while maintaining no-system-model requirements.  Furthermore, our solution features fast computation times, with humans able to set security parameters and have them implemented in under 2 milliseconds.  We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using simulation studies involving a 7-degrees-of-freedom robotic limb, and provide all relevant code and simulation data in open-source form for the convenience of other researchers.

Despite significant advancements in neural networks, numerous applications still demonstrate the efficacy of established methods. The challenge of text summarization presents an interesting case, as our research reveals that a straightforward graph-based approach can rival state-of-the-art performance on the popular Reuters-21578 and ArguMon datasets, achieving competitive results to recent cutting-edge models. We enhance the performance of our basic model by incorporating refined graph construction, graph quantization, and learning-based optimization techniques. Furthermore, our analysis shows that the temporal structure of news articles poses a particular difficulty for deep neural networks, whereas our graph-based method is equally effective whether applied to short stories or financial news. We attribute our success to three key factors: the inherent temporal relationships in news articles, which facilitate comprehension through linear structure; the ability of graph-based models to focus on core information; and the scarcity of redundant information in news summaries, which simplifies the summarization task.

Researchers have introduced an innovative approach to studying Bose-Einstein condensates by applying a quantum-inspired nonlinear operator to solve the associated Schrödinger equation. This operator mimics the behavior of Dirac's plane wave solution, which is based on the method of coherent states. Using this new operator, researchers have derived exact solutions to nonlinear Schrödinger equations for both defocusing and focusing types, which have significant implications in quantum mechanics and optics. Notably, this approach may lead to novel, patterned Bose-Einstein condensate creation methods.

This paper builds on previous research by Cao and Yuan, expanding on their results by considering different scenarios, such as the case of complex spaces or algebraic spaces, and establishing new theorems on the distinctness of meromorphic mappings.

In recent years, the nondegenerate region of a polynomial system, where a specific sign pattern prevails, has gained significant interest. Moreover, novel methods for its calculation are being continuously proposed. Our presentation focuses on a specific technique to determine the nondegenerate region through signatures in the context of elimination sets, building on top of existing works in [Bubis, Chen, Kuipers arXiv 1709.06047, 2017] and [Dolan, Kouchnirenko arXiv 1901.02791, 2019].

The PHENIX experiment detected photons produced by the collision of gold ions at an energy of 200 GeV, and found that a large number of fast photons were produced. These high-energy photons are often used to investigate the properties of the matter that constitutes the nucleus, but can also be produced by other sources such as the interaction of charged particles and transverse momenta. This study, however, required that participant photons be counted based on the number of times the nucleons in the nucleus interacted with each other. It found that when using this new standard, the number of photons produced by the interaction of copper ions at lower momentum levels matches predictions from theoretical models, but is lower than what was seen in the interaction of gold ions at the same energy level. Additionally, the study found that when using this new standard, the number of photons produced by the interaction of copper ions at lower momentum levels does not change as the number of particles produced increases or decreases in momentum levels. These findings are significant because they establish a new standard for assessing the participation of nucleons in the interaction, and shows agreement with predictions from theoretical models in a specific case, while also revealing discrepancies with previous results.

Our goal is to hide a preselected $r$-extremal configuration in a probability measure that governs the distribution of distance vectors from a randomly selected point in a certain $n$-dimensional cube. The distance between two points in this cube is measured using the $\ell_2$-metric. Turan initially inquired about finding the ideal distribution, and later, Szabo raised the question about determining the minimum required density for this ideal distribution. We provide an answer to the latter question by showing that a certain density threshold exists below which no r-extremal configuration can be fully embedded within any $n$-dimensional cube.

When displaying line connections on vector maps, aliasing occurs, which is particularly noticeable in maps that have a high scale (zoom level) and feature intricate patterns, such as roads and vegetation. This issue is more apparent due to the inherent limitations of rendering lines. A commonly employed anti-aliasing technique, called alpha-blending, has several drawbacks, including accelerating up the screen frame rate slowly and not considering line endpoints when drawing. Therefore, a more efficient anti-aliasing method was developed to eliminate these limitations. This system works by combining lines into groups and applying an efficient rendering algorithm to reduce artifacts and improve visual representation. Specifically, a temporary pixel buffer is used to collect lines from a single group, and the optimized alpha-blending technique is employed by sorting points in a shader. Experimental results indicate that this technique yields comparable effects to current anti-aliasing methods while delivering superior performance. Additionally, this system's modular design allows it to be applied to various rendering pipelines with minimal modifications.

Recently, a numerical solution for the 2D heterogeneous elliptic boundary value problem was proposed using a transcendental rational basis function. However, the initial method introduced an $L_2$ stable operator without a forcing term. Yet, in our study, a novel form-conserving quasi-interpolation operator handling a forcing term is presented, with an added advantage of employing a transcendental RBF for the first time. We demonstrate in our analysis that the new operator based on this transcendental RBF possesses not only $L_2$ but also $W_2^1$-norm stability. Furthermore, we investigate the degree of smoothness of the domain and derive error estimates for an specific discretization of the elliptic problem involving a heterogeneous coefficient, also providing a detailed error analysis in the case of a constant coefficient.

High-energy gamma-ray emission from pulsar wind nebulae is produced by accelerated charged particles.  The brightest of these features, like the Crab Nebula, consist of a central pulsar wind nebula and surrounding synchrotron emission regions.  Researchers have discovered a new object at 83 million light years from Earth, a circular gamma-ray source in the constellation Tauus called 2Tauu PWN.  The novel structure has a distinctive ring-like shape and is significantly larger than most other pulsar wind nebulae, with a diameter of approximately 1 degree.  The observed gamma-ray emission is thought to be the remains of a massive supernova explosion that formed a large cloud of accelerated particles from a distant pulsar wind nebula system.  The new source is one of the largest known pulsar wind nebulae in our galaxy, with a large volume of emission, and its study could provide valuable insights into large-scale particle acceleration processes.

Given the instability of the weather, accurately classifying the atmospheric conditions from an image remains challenging. A recently proposed dataset consisting of 286,622 labeled images captures the variability of the world's climates through image sequences spanning a decade in duration for each location on the planet with a view factor of over 85°, spanning from -23° to +75°. A newly developed super-pixel based resizing method, SPR, for small images, produces higher quality outputs with enhanced detail. A comprehensive analysis of Convolutional Neural Networks was conducted, involving the use of benchmark datasets, namely ImageNet and CIFAR-32, to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach, SPCN, which surpasses current state-of-the-art climate classification models with a notable 42% improvement. A 40% rise in accuracy was achieved through the integration of global average pooling and residual blocks into the network. Furthermore, a reduction of  10% in memory usage was enabled by the incorporation of dilated layers and  a decrease of 15% in the number of network layers through the inclusion of early rejection, resulting in the SpCN architecture, which boasts a notable 1.5 times the efficiency of state-of-the-art methods while producing more accurate outputs.

The project's primary objective is to investigate the reciprocal influence of social norms in the fields of research, environmental policy, and economics that pertain to climate change. These interconnected areas of study are crucial to understanding the social contract's dynamic response to global warming. Our focus lies within the US climate change discourse and we seek to uncover the underlying principles governing the mutual influence of research findings, political decisions, and market reactions to climate change evidence. To this end, we develop a network model that incorporates key entities and their interactions, and apply descriptive analytics to extract results. The study also yields numerous practical applications and raises fundamental questions about the coherence of social norms and their potential irreversibility.

Soft robotic grippers excel at handling delicate objects, but accurately simulating their behavior under various loads remains a significant challenge, preventing them from being used in machine learning applications. To address this limitation, a novel multi-fingered soft gripper model was developed using Bayesian neural networks. By incorporating the Koopman operator approach in a regression framework, the dynamic model was expanded to include velocity information, enabling prediction of both position and velocity. The efficacy of this model was demonstrated through regression-based control of a modular soft robotic gripper, where its accuracy outperformed several other models after being trained with limited data.

Inspired by the universal adoption of stochastic gradient descent (SGD), a comprehensive analysis of the organic generalization ability of SGD is conducted across various datasets and models. Our investigation of SGD's performance reveals that it can produce reliable predictions, and, when combined with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), it exhibits exceptional accuracy in large-scale image classification tasks. Furthermore, a formal analysis of SGD's convergence is developed, building upon the existing theoretical framework, and, by refining existing proofs, the convergence of CNNs utilizing SGD is validated, resulting in a unified understanding of the technique's effectiveness.

High-energy emissions from ancient galaxies can be attributed to multiple theories, including the possibility that the radiation is powered by star formation or the activity of an actively accreting black hole. A particular galaxy, J2102+6015, was initially identified as a highly energetic object due to its strong gamma-ray emissions, and subsequent studies revealed that the galaxy is located at a distant time in the universe's history, specifically around z = 4.575. Recent observations using the Very Large Array at 1 millimeter wavelength provided the necessary data to resolve the galaxy into two distinct objects, and as a result, the original study reexamined the radio data. The resulting analysis revealed that the radio emissions can be attributed to one of the objects, and a reevaluation of the galaxy's emissions revealed that the emissions are consistent with a star-powered origin.

Accurate diagnosis of Non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) is crucial for proper treatment and prognosis. Despite positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) being the gold standard for lymph node staging, it has limitations in tumor subtypes and stages. Recent research has shown that deep learning models using PET-CT images alone can achieve satisfactory results. However, these models may not be robust against data discrepancies and interpretability is a significant concern. To address these issues, we introduce Multi-Modal Education (MME), a deep learning framework that integrates PET-CT and pathological information to improve NSCLC prediction. The MME framework, composed of two modules, generates informative noise and produces Lymph Node Malignancy Scores (LNMS) based on multiple outputs. By combining these modules with a multi-task approach that includes lung cancer classification and regression, we overcome data discrepancies and leverage the complementary information from multiple data sources. The experimental results show that MME achieves state-of-the-art performance on lung cancer and LNMS prediction, outshining existing pet-CT and pathological model performance.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) has been successfully integrated into various natural language tasks.  Despite state description playing a vital role in the learning process, many NLP applications still lack standardized methods for representing task states.  This paper explores multiple methods for natural language state description that favor exploration over memorization, encompassing both data-driven and symbolic approaches.  To compare these methods, NLStateDesc, a unified platform for NLP state descriptions, has been developed.  By conducting comprehensive evaluations using multiple benchmark domains and benchmark sets, the current best practices in natural language state descriptions can be identified.  The associated repository includes demo codes for each method, enabling reproducibility.

A novel method utilizing machine learning and big data is presented to calculate the energy spectrum of stars and galaxies from observed spectra of their emission. This technique, called SpecSpectraNet, applies a data-driven approach to reconstruct the energy spectrum of an object using its observed spectrum and a model of its temperature structure, which is based on prior knowledge. SpecSpectraNet is composed of two parts: a predictor that generates the energy spectrum of an object and a differentiator that identifies objects with abnormal energy spectra. To train SpecSpectraNet, the model is fed a large database of synthetic spectra, including the calibration step for the training, using Gaussian processes for optimization. By employing this model, the hard boundaries of spectral models are removed, enabling the use of the training data to directly inform the energy spectrum calculations. This approach is advantageous for complex objects like quasars and their applications are discussed.

This paper examines specific simple Lie algebras, $\frak g$, generated by a Lie derivative operator and sets forth conditions for a finite-dimensional module over the algebra $U(\frak h)$ to be ad-excluded, meaning it can't be represented as an ad^{\frak g}-module. Additionally, we identify the characteristics of ad-excluded modules within the context of infinite-dimensional simple Lie algebras, specifically those representing derivation operator Lie algebras, and provide relevant examples and counterexamples.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter can be
challenging due to the numerous abbreviations, slang and uncommon words used in
tweets. These words are often outside the scope of standard dictionaries. To overcome
this issue, a novel sentiment analysis approach utilizing an Long Short-Term Memory
(LSTM) network and Word2Vec for the analysis of unsupervised learning of short text
was presented. Performance was evaluated using standard metrics including F1 score,
Precision and Recall on the Twitter Sentiment Dataset. Our technique surpasses the
current state-of-the-art models in sentiment analysis of short text with a notable
 improvement of 5% in F1 score.

Recent breakthroughs in open-domain conversation models using large language models have achieved notable success through the implementation of conversation frameworks that define roles to facilitate a structured discussion. Within this context, our research focuses on the establishment of a role-defined open-domain conversation framework with two participants: a human and a large language model. The model's capabilities are evaluated in terms of open-ended conversations and user preferences. Additionally, we examine the efficacy of varying conversation framework designs and provide actionable suggestions for future improvement. The convention of our study is aligned with the standards set by the ConverseTest benchmark, which aims to establish uniform criteria for assessing conversational performance.

The universe's horizon expands, causing any gravitational wave launched during the Big Bang to become non-localized and persist to this day, creating a background of random gravitational waves with a specific power spectrum. This phenomenon has been confirmed by solving the Einstein equations in the early universe on a specific scale, and the resulting random gravitational waves memory effect will be imprinted on primordial black holes formed from early universe perturbations, providing a unique channel for this phenomenon to be observed. This, in turn, will allow us to understand the early universe's physical states through the properties of these black holes.

Our model involves a D-brane collision that triggers SUSY breaking in the early universe, resulting in the creation of PeV-scale neutralinos that decay into high-energy gamma-ray spectra, supporting the interpretation of the MAGIC Collaboration's finding of ultra-high energy gamma rays. These neutralinos also produce large-scale gravity waves, and the total power density of these waves is expected to be in the range of $10^{-15}-10^{-14}$ GeV/cm^3. This model is consistent with observations of the Galactic Center's gamma-ray excess, and the predicted parameters are in line with those required for reproducing the Galactic Center's gamma-ray excess and the observed tension in $(g-2)_\mu$.

A fundamental inquiry in multiple disciplines, including neuroscience and artificial intelligence, is the inquiry into the causal nature of the world. Both fields face the daunting challenge of deciphering the intricate web of causality and developing innovative methods to navigate this complexity. From a neurological standpoint, the brain's causal model is thought to be shaped by the dynamic interplay of symbolic and neural processes, necessitating novel methodologies that can seamlessly integrate symbolic and neural elements. In contrast, advances in artificial intelligence have led to the development of data-driven and symbolic causal inference techniques, although often in isolation from their neurological counterparts. To address this disparity, we are integrating the knowledge from both realms by developing a symbolic causal inference framework that employs a signaling game to model complex, high-level causal interactions and drive machine learning. Our approach emerges as a collaborative outcome of symbolic and neural processes, where the symbolic representation of a causal model serves as a blueprint for neural processes to build an accurate causal understanding of the world. The proposed framework is having a positive impact on both artificial intelligence and neuroscience, demonstrating great potential for further applications and innovation.

Information retrieval technology has expanded rapidly into various industries, 
and term forecasting has become an essential component in IR systems, enabling 
efficient document indexing and retrieval after data collection. The term 
distribution model employed significantly influences the overall performance
